messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: detected p99 SLO breach for streaming endpoint /v1/stream (SSE) in eu-west-1. Rolling 5m p99 = 2.4s (SLO 1.5s). Client disconnects noted, some 502/504 seen at edge. Pager: @alice-oncall. Dashboards: <https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/streaming-slo>. Runbook: /runbooks/streaming-tail-latency.

alice-oncall: I'm on it. starting triage — can folks drop signal: which proxies + versions are routing this traffic? any recent deploys? :rotating_light:

ryan: seeing a spike in chunking stalls on proxy host pool eu-proxy-3/4. Errors in the proxy logs: 
```
ERROR write stall: client_write_queue=1200 pending_kv=64 last_write=12500ms
WARN upstream: idle connection timeout after 30s
```
requests per second also up ~2.5x for AcmeCorp (heavy streaming).

eli-sre: no platform deploys in the last 24h. Autoscaler did a scale-up ~20m ago for model-serving, might have shifted routing. I'll pull traces.

maya-infra: noticed proxy keepalive hits at capacity, connection resets increase. kernel tcp_write_queue_len creeping on proxy nodes. suspect slow consumers -> write buffer backlog -> proxies hitting internal timeouts.

sam-pm: confirmed multiple downstream engineers reported user sessions dropping for AcmeCorp chat flows. Customer impact: some dropped messages and failed uploads. escalated to success.

jordan-eng: quick mitigation idea: toggle streaming fallback to chunked-plain (non-SSE) for AcmeCorp via routing policy to reduce persistent connections. Can we do that short-term?

alice-oncall: good call. @maya-infra can you open a routing rule to force non-streaming fallback for the AcmeCorp tenant id for 15m? we need to reduce long-lived sockets.

maya-infra: creating the policy now. pseudo-curl to apply: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood/route-policies -d '{"filter":"tenant:acme","force_mode":"polling"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
I will patch and monitor.

ryan: while that's deploying, I pushed a quick proxy config tweak to increase write buffer threshold and extend idle keepalive to 60s on eu-proxy-*. ``changed config -> reload``. watching if write stalls reduce.

lee-support: logged customer-facing update to AcmeCorp support ticket. message: "We are investigating increased streaming disconnects; temporary fallback may be enabled. We'll follow up in 15 minutes."

eli-sre: pulling distributed traces — tail traces show long waits inside proxy write loop at the fanout stage, client ack delay is primary. p95 ~700ms, p99 ~2.4s. queue length correlates with number of unique sockets per connection.

alice-oncall: status check in 10. If routing policy reduces long-lived sockets, that should drop p99. If not, next steps: drain proxy pool and rotate.

( approx +6m )

maya-infra: routing rule applied. Confirmed ~AcmeCorp traffic now on fallback mode -> downstream shows more short-poll requests instead of SSE.

ryan: proxies reloaded, immediate reduction in write queue backlog on eu-proxy-3. p99 trending down to 1.1s on 1m window. still watching for flapping.

sam-pm: AcmeCorp support notified: they saw fewer disconnects after fallback. asked for timeline for full mitigation.

jordan-eng: note: fallback reduces UX but keeps messages flowing. We should schedule a patch to proxy to better handle bursty slow consumers (long-term fix).

eli-sre: creating an incident timeline and initial RCA stub. suspected cause: combination of traffic spike from AcmeCorp + proxies exhausted write buffers + consumer-side backpressure (slow clients) leading to head-of-line write stalls and timeouts.

alice-oncall: action items:
- maya-infra: keep fallback in place until 03:00 UTC or until p99 stable < 1.5s for 30m.
- ryan + jordan-eng: investigate kernel/tcp tuning and proxy write path; propose short patch + test in canary.
- eli-sre: begin post-incident doc + collect traces/logs.
- lee-support: send a follow-up to AcmeCorp summarizing mitigation and ETA.

( handoff )

alice-oncall: handing off to eli-sre for overnight watch and remediation tracking. Next oncall: @eli-sre acknowledged. I'll leave the routing rule in place; maya, please keep me posted if you need escalation. :white_check_mark:

eli-sre: acknowledged. picking up monitoring. created /incidents/8280001234/ops-doc with notes and links to traces. will update on-call log with status every 30m.

maya-infra: leaving a note in infra logs: "applied tenant fallback at 8280001290; increased keepalive & write-buffer thresholds on eu-proxy pool; monitor for tcp queue growth."

ryan: quick debug snippet I captured from proxy (for the postmortem): 
```
# tail /var/log/proxy/eu-proxy-3.log | grep "write stall"
[2026-06-14T17:20:12Z] write stall: client=10.1.2.33:54321 queued=1240 wait_ms=14200
[2026-06-14T17:20:13Z] write stall: client=10.1.2.44:44321 queued=1187 wait_ms=13000
```
we should correlate with socket stats and client ack histograms.

lee-support: will prepare customer-facing summary and propose next steps.

eli-sre: marking initial severity as P1->P2 after fallback shows sustained recovery. will keep channel open until stable and then record timeline in postmortem.

alice-oncall: thanks team. handoff complete. last update for this thread at 8280001560.
